title: What threat modelling is and when to do it

videos.script: A clinic's patient portal lets people book a session, pay for it and upload their exams. Somebody wrote it carefully. The queries are parameterised. The passwords are hashed. {{careful}} And the payment webhook believes any request that says a payment went through. Nobody wrote a bug there. The design never asked who was allowed to say so. {{webhook}} No code review finds that, because the code does exactly what it was asked to do. It is found by asking a question before the code exists. What are we building, and what can go wrong with it? {{questions}} That is threat modelling. Four questions, asked about a drawing, by the people who will build the thing. {{four}} This course asks them about one system, the portal of a small chain of clinics, in fifteen lessons. Today you meet the questions, learn when to ask them, and set up the workspace where the model will live. {{workspace}}
